| What students learn | Why it matters |
|:--|:--|
| Use Linux and Python together for everyday computing, technical work and small automations. | Students learn the operating system by using it to understand their computer, manage files, publish work, analyze measurements and solve repeated problems. |

**Subsections:** Desktop use; files and permissions; command line; software; version control; publishing; data analysis; basic networking; services; backup and recovery

**Coming out of this section, students can:** Install and use Linux, write useful Python programs, manage files and permissions, publish a website, analyze measurements, check basic networking and complete basic administration.

## Everyday project spine

Python begins early and returns throughout the unit. Each project should be small enough to finish, useful enough to keep and clear enough to explain.

| Project | Everyday purpose | Main skills |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **My Computer Report** | Create a readable report of the computer's operating system, processor, memory, storage, hostname and Python version. | Linux GUI, terminal, `platform`, `shutil`, formatted output |
| **Downloads Folder Helper** | Preview how files could be grouped by type, then organize only a teacher-approved practice folder. | Paths, files, `pathlib`, loops, dry-run safety |
| **Storage and Backup Checker** | Report free space and confirm that an important project folder has a backup copy. | Storage, `shutil.disk_usage`, timestamps, verification |
| **Personal Technical Website** | Publish Linux notes, project documentation, screenshots and later graphs. | Git, Markdown, Quarto, GitHub Pages |
| **Everyday Data Logger** | Record a useful repeated measurement such as battery level, computer temperature, task time, voltage, current or room conditions. | Python, CSV, timestamps, units, privacy |
| **Graph and Model** | Plot the logged data and fit a justified relationship such as voltage versus current. | Matplotlib, curve fitting, residuals, interpretation |
| **Connection Check** | Check the hostname, local address and whether an approved website or host responds. | Networking, Python, terminal, error handling |
| **Raspberry Pi Utility** | Move one useful program to a Raspberry Pi and add a sensor, output, scheduled task or remote interface. | Power, Linux, Python, Git, SSH, tmux |

Students keep these projects in one Git repository and publish selected results on the same Quarto website. The projects grow together instead of disappearing after each lesson.

## Suggested timing

| Stage | School days |
|:--|--:|
| Choose a distribution, install Linux Mint and set up WSL or Mac access | 2 |
| Accounts, customization, hardware inventory, software and Bashcrawl | 2 |
| Files, terminal, permissions and Git | 2 |
| Build, test and publish a Quarto website | 3 |
| Python data logging | 2 |
| Graphing, analysis and introductory curve fitting | 2 |
| Networking, SSH and tmux | 1 |
| Power calculations and Raspberry Pi readiness | 1 |
| **Recommended total** | **15** |

Keep one or two additional flex days available for hardware problems, absent students, deployment delays and revision. WSL and macOS instructions are included in the installation lesson instead of being treated as a separate unit.

## Teacher preparation before day 1

1. Inventory every iMac, Mac mini, laptop, monitor, keyboard, mouse, network adapter and power cable.
2. Record each exact model and whether each Mac is Intel-based or Apple silicon. Test boot instructions on the actual model instead of assuming every Mac behaves the same way.
3. Match and label power cables before assigning computers. Quarantine equipment with missing, damaged or questionable power hardware.
4. Build and test one complete Linux Mint computer before preparing the rest of the lab.
5. Verify USB boot, Wi-Fi or Ethernet, sound, display, keyboard, storage, sleep, restart and shutdown.
6. Install and test Git, Quarto, Python, `htop`, SSH and tmux on the approved classroom image.
7. Decide the hostname pattern and keep a private teacher inventory connecting each hostname to its physical computer.
8. Prepare the recovery account, installer USB drives, one spare tested computer and a recovery plan.
9. Test the complete student path once: account creation, Bashcrawl, Git commit, Quarto render, GitHub Pages deployment, Python graph, SSH connection and tmux reattachment.
